'''''Nagatitan''''' ({{lit|[[Nāga]] giant}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[euhelopodid]] sauropod dinosaur known from the [[Early Cretaceous]] ([[Aptian]]–[[Albian]] ages) [[Khok Kruat Formation]] of Thailand. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis''''', known from a partial skeleton. ''Nagatitan'' is a large sauropod, with an estimated body length of {{convert|27|m|ft}} and mass of approximately {{convert|27|t|ST}}, making it the largest dinosaur known from Southeast Asia.

== Discovery and naming ==
[[File:Khok Kruat Formation, Thailand.png|thumb|left|Location of the Ban Pha Nang Sua locality (orange star) in Thailand]]
The ''Nagatitan'' fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the [[Khok Kruat Formation]] in [[Chaiyaphum province]], Thailand by Thanom Luangnan on the bank of a pond in 2016.<ref name="Press" /> The specimen is housed in the [[Sirindhorn Museum]], where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimens SM2025-1-546 to SM2025-1-556. The specimen consists of several vertebrae, parts of the pelvis, and parts of the forelimb and hindlimb.<ref name="Nagatitan" />

In 2026, Thitiwoot Sethapanichsakul and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Nagatitan chaiyaphumensis'' as a new genus and species of sauropod dinosaur based on these fossil remains, establishing SM2025-1-546–556 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Nagatitan'', combines a reference to the mythical serpetine [[Nāga]] in Asian cultures, with the word "titan" ({{lit|giant}}), a common suffix for sauropod names, referencing the [[Titans|pre-Olympian gods]] of [[Greek mythology]]. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''chaiyaphumensis'', references the discovery of the species in Chaiyaphum, Thailand.<ref name="Nagatitan" />

== Description ==
[[File:Nagatitan Size Comparison.svg|thumb|Size compared to a human]]
To estimate the body mass and overall body length of ''Nagatitan'', Sethapanichsakul et al. (2026) used calculations derived from measurements of the bones. The body mass was calculated using the minimum shaft circumference of the [[humerus]] ({{cvt|58.4|cm|in}}) and [[femur]] ({{cvt|68.2|cm|in}}), yielding a mass of {{convert|26,582|kg|lb}}. The overall body length was calculated at about {{convert|27.2|m|ft}}.<ref name="Nagatitan" />

== Classification ==
To test the affinities and relationships of ''Nagatitan'', Sethapanichsakul and colleagues (2026) included it in an expanded version of the [[phylogenetic]] matrix of Díez Díaz et al. (2025).<ref name="DiezDiaz2025" /> Using both equal character weighting and (b) extended [[implied weighting]], ''Nagatitan'' was recovered within the [[somphospondylan]] [[titanosauriform]] family [[Euhelopodidae]]. Using equal weighting, it was placed as the [[sister taxon]] to ''[[Europatitan]]''—a European taxon not generally regarded as a member of this otherwise Asian clade—at the base of Euhelopodidae. Using implied weighting, ''Europatitan'' shifted outside of this clade, while ''Nagatitan'' was placed in a more euhelopodid [[Basal (phylogenetics)|derived]] position, diverging after ''[[Tangvayosaurus]]'' but before ''[[Phuwiangosaurus]]''. == Paleobiology ==
[[File:Khok Pha Suam locality, Thailand.jpg|thumb|Paleoenvironmental reconstruction of the Khok Kraut Formation (Khok Pha Suam locality)]]
''Nagatitan'' is known from the Khok Kraut Formation, which dates to the [[Aptian]] to [[Albian]] ages of the end of the [[Early Cretaceous]]. Many other dinosaurs have been described from this formation, including indeterminate (unnamed) [[titanosauriform]]s, the [[ornithopod]]s ''[[Ratchasimasaurus]]'', ''[[Siamodon]]'', and ''[[Sirindhorna]]'', the early [[ceratopsian]] ''[[Psittacosaurus sattayaraki]]'', the [[carcharodontosauria]]n ''[[Siamraptor]]'', and indeterminate [[spinosaurid]] bones. Non-dinosaurian taxa from this region include the [[crocodyliform]] ''[[Khoratosuchus]]'', in addition to remains of a [[pterodactyloid]] pterosaur, [[adocid]] and [[carettochelyid]] turtles, and [[halecomorph]], [[ginglymodian]], and [[hybodontiform]] fishes. Outcrops of the [[Grès Supérieurs Formation]] in Laos are considered to be equivalent to those of the Khok Kruat Formation, and have yielded dinosaurs including the titanosauriform ''[[Tangvayosaurus]]'', the ornithopod ''[[Mandschurosaurus]]'', and the spinosaurid ''[[Ichthyovenator]]''.<ref name="Manitkoon2022" />
